name: salvaged solar panel tilted on a scrap frame: cracked blue cell grid top surface facing the sky, metal edge and short legs
label: wasteland_ruins/solar-scrap

surfaces.part: tilted solar panel cell grid (main body)
scrap frame lower bar and legs

answer.evidence: Rows 0-9 are a blue cell-grid panel that widens from 26 to 32 px going down, which reads as a tilted top surface. Row 10 is a light metal front-edge line (#8ca29d) in all three scanned columns, followed by a dark shadow row 11 (#516268). Below that, rows 11-13 form the frame's front bar, and rows 14-15 are narrow 8 px legs, so the front face and supports total about 5 rows. The panel is the main body, and its top is clearly visible. This matches the green reference examples, where a top surface ends in an edge line and shadow above the front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts support the candidate. It has 14 visible tones per 16x16 tile, against 9 for the hedge, 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the roofed well. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no 5x5 flat fills. Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted. By eye, the outline is a dark navy that leans toward the blue cells, and the metal frame is separated by value rather than a black line. The blue cell grid is built from about 4-5 lightness steps, with lighter highlight cells, dark grid seams and crack marks that give grain. The frame edge and the short legs have their own highlight and shadow tones. It is slightly shallower than the best references, with fewer steps on the legs and frame. At this scale, though, it sits comfortably next to the hedge and bench in richness and does not read as a flat sticker.
